interface.name: jam_window_memory_v1

description.summary: windows that come back to their places

interface.description:
Jam OS's own protocol (docs/G1-PLAN.md, "As built: the compositor remembers the arrangement"). When the compositor is restarted its clients connect again and make their windows again, in whatever order they happen to; this lets each window go back where it was (its screen, its place in the tiles, its floating box, minimised or not).
The compositor gives each toplevel that asks a key: 64 random bits, told only to the window's own client. The client keeps it and, after a reconnect, presents it for the window it makes again before that window's initial commit. A key the compositor remembers (from before its restart, and not taken yet) puts the window in its old place, and the same key is answered; any other key, or none, gets a new one and the window is placed as a new window. A key is taken once: a second window presenting it is a new window. The worst a client can do with a key is put its own window in a place one of its own windows had.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Keys already given stay with their windows.

request.name: identify
request.description: Ask for the toplevel's key, presenting the one it had before a reconnect (key_hi and key_lo both 0: none). Sent before the toplevel's initial commit, a remembered key places it where it was; sent later it only gets a key. Answered by the key event. A toplevel asked about again keeps the key it has.

event.name: key
event.description: The toplevel's key, to be presented after a reconnect. The toplevel is null if the client destroyed it meanwhile.
